topic: Building a Production-Ready ML Pipeline (Titanic Walkthrough)
headline: Stop watching tutorials. Build THIS today.
caption:
Stop watching tutorials. Build THIS today. 👇

Watching tutorials gives you the illusion of progress.

Copying cell after cell in a messy Jupyter Notebook might feel like you're learning, but hiring managers see right through it. They don't want notebook-copying students; they want engineers who can write robust, reproducible, and production-ready code.

Today, we are breaking out of tutorial hell. We are taking the classic Titanic dataset and building a clean, end-to-end ML pipeline in Python using software engineering Best Practices.

In today's carousel, I break down:
1️⃣ The Problem: The trap of 'Notebook spaghetti'
2️⃣ The Data & Preprocessing Pipeline
3️⃣ The Model: Training a Random Forest cleanly
4️⃣ Evaluation & Serialization for production
5️⃣ What to submit to your GitHub portfolio to stand out

Swipe left to see the code and build your first real portfolio pipeline! 💻👇

What's your go-to framework for structuring ML pipelines? Tell me below! 👇
